scenes.say: Ever wonder how Node.js keeps your code fast and non-blocking, even with lots of async tasks?
The event loop has several phases. Timers run scheduled callbacks. Pending callbacks handle system events. Poll waits for I O. Check runs setImmediate callbacks.

scenes.label: libuv
scenes.sub: libuv lets Node.js handle heavy I O in the background.
scenes.say: Libuv is the secret sauce. It lets Node.js offload heavy I O work to a thread pool, so the main loop stays fast.
Here's a classic example. Timer and immediate callbacks run in different phases. But their order isn't guaranteed—especially if you call them inside I O callbacks.

scenes.question: Does setTimeout always run before setImmediate?
scenes.right: No, their order can vary depending on context, especially after I O.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Does setTimeout always run before setImmediate? Nope! Their order can change, especially after I O.
